$comment: See host.schema.json's own $comment for why every field lives inside the `network:` object, name included. cidr is required only when there is no `extends`.

network.description: A network: one CIDR shared identically by every team -- never templated per team. Hosts and containers are attached to it from an environment's topology, not from here; a network file never mentions what's on it.

name.description: Unique name for this network, referenced from an environment's topology and from other objects' `depends_on`.

cidr.description: The network's CIDR (e.g. "10.0.1.0/24"), identical for every team. Combined with each copy's `last_octet` to produce that copy's address.

visible_from.description: The other networks (by name) allowed to reach this one, enforced as ACLs on the OVN routing host. Default-deny: with no `visible_from`, no other network can reach this one. E.g. a client network with `visible_from: [vdi]` is reachable from the VDI network and nothing else. Each entry must be a defined network.

vars.description: Key/value data cascaded down to every host and container on this network.

tags.description: Labels for searching, grouping, and ad-hoc targeting.

findings.description: Findings that belong to this network specifically.
findings.example:
findings:
  - severity: 3
    difficulty: 2
    description: Flat network, no segmentation between servers

extends.description: Name of another network this one extends. The base is deep-merged in: `cidr` the child sets wins, otherwise it's inherited; vars/tags merge key-by-key (child wins a clash); visible_from is the base's plus the child's (de-duplicated). `cidr` becomes optional here since it's inherited.
